title: Telemetry & Trace Pipeline Deep Dive: token-level metrics, KV batching, quant & VPC - Verdant Systems
summary: Deep technical review of integrating Redwood token-level tracing with Verdant's telemetry stack. Covered span/schema design, sampling, OpenTelemetry collector config, token metric volume handling, KV cache instrumentation, batching tradeoffs, quantization effects on latency/quality, and VPC/on-prem connection patterns. Agreed next steps: share trace schema, run a 1-hour token-level benchmark, and provide security docs for VPC deployment.
topics: Collector and exporter sizing (OTLP/grpc vs HTTP/protobuf)
Token metrics cardinality and sampling strategies
KV cache instrumentation and hit/miss tracing
Batching impact on p99 latency vs throughput
Quantization QA: accuracy vs latency tradeoffs
VPC/private deployments: peering, mTLS, KMS/HSM considerations
Dashboard and alerting recommendations (token cost dashboards, latency SLOs)
action_items: Samir Patel: Send proposed OTEL span schema (token-level attributes + model/version) and benchmark plan - due 2025-10-24
Elena Ortiz: Share Redwood collector config templates (OTLP/grpc + batching examples) and sample dashboard panels - due 2025-10-24
Maya Chen: Provide sample prompt mix and target p50/p95/p99 SLOs for pilot - due 2025-10-27
Adeel Khan: Confirm legal/regulatory constraints for sending traces off-prem (if any) and list acceptable exporters - due 2025-10-28
next_steps: Redwood to run 1-hour token-level benchmark on Verdant sample workload (sched week of 10/27)
Share security whitepaper + SOC2 + private deployment checklist
Set up trial VPC peering demo and a short runbook for collector auth (mTLS + token)
Follow-up session to review benchmark results and dashboard panels
transcript:
[00:00:00] Samir Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we planned a deep dive into telemetry and traces for token-level insights. we have about 70 minutes, so we should be able to get through schema, sampling and a bench plan.
[00:00:12] Maya Chen: Great, thanks. we've been seeing weird variability at p99 when the KV cache churns, so we're hoping token-level tracing can pinpoint hot paths.
[00:00:25] Elena Ortiz: Totally, and quick note — some names in our docs get transcribed oddly, so i'll try to spell out fields. we'll show a proposed span layout that keeps trace sizes reasonable.
[00:00:40] Carlos Ruiz: Quick qual: are we talking about attaching a span per token? that sounds huge. how do you avoid exploding the backend?
[00:00:52] Jonas Meyer: Good question. We typically avoid a literal span-per-token for long sequences; our approach uses token-level metrics emitted as enriched span attributes plus optional child spans for interesting events (cache miss, prompt fetch). sampling + aggregation at collector reduces volume.
[00:01:07] Maya Chen: can you explain what you mean by "enriched attributes"?
[00:01:12] Elena Ortiz: yeah so instead of a thousand spans we have one request span with attributes like token_count, first_token_latency_ms, kv_cache_hits, kv_cache_misses and a token_histogram proto that the collector can unpack. that keeps trace depth low but still lets dashboards rollup token statistics. sometimes the transcriber turns "histogram" into "his Stan" sorry.
[00:01:34] Adeel Khan: from security standpoint, any PII possibility in token payloads? we need redaction and maybe local aggregation before exporting.
[00:01:41] Samir Patel: Absolutely — we recommend scrubbing at the runtime layer before exporter; Redwood supports configurable redaction plugins and we can run the collector inside the VPC so spans never leave unencrypted.
[00:01:55] Carlos Ruiz: about sampling — is it head-based or tail-based? we care about p99 tails.
[00:02:02] Jonas Meyer: We do a hybrid: head-based to reduce noise but we also have tail-sampling in collector to keep high-latency outliers for p99 analysis. tail-sampling policy can be tuned to select traces with high token_count or high latency. note this adds collector complexity.
[00:02:20] Maya Chen: okay, how about payload size? our current OTLP collector struggles when we stream token arrays as attributes.
[00:02:29] Elena Ortiz: that's why we prefer compressed proto blobs for dense token histograms, and then rely on OTLP/grpc with max message sizes tuned. another trick is incremental metrics instead of per-request full token lists — e.g., counters + sketches.
[00:02:45] Carlos Ruiz: KV cache tracing — what does that look like? we use Redis and a small in-memory LRU for hot keys.
[00:02:54] Jonas Meyer: for Redis L1/L2 we recommend emitting light-weight events on miss/hit with a small set of attributes: key_bucket (hashed prefix), latency_ms, payload_size, model_variant. for heavy flows we sample payloads. and we instrument TTL refreshes because they often cause thundering cascades.
[00:03:10] Priya Nair: do you recommend tagging spans with model quantization level? we have several quantized variants and want to compare perf and quality.
[00:03:18] Samir Patel: yes — model_variant and quant_level should be top-level attributes. that lets you break down latency by quantization level in dashboards. also keep a quality metric (e.g., eval_score or BLEU-like proxy) emitted occasionally so you can correlate latency gains with quality regressions.
[00:03:35] Carlos Ruiz: related to batching: we saw batching reduce cost a lot but introduced some p99 spikes. what's the right balance?
[00:03:43] Elena Ortiz: batching is workload dependent. Redwood has continuous batching with deadline thresholds: a small hold time (ms) to accumulate tokens improves throughput but p99 can spike if you over-wait. we recommend adaptive deadlines and per-route batching configs visible in the console. also instrument batch_size distribution in the trace.
[00:03:58] Maya Chen: what about kernel-level scheduling — does Redwood expose kernel selection logs so we can trace slow kernels?
[00:04:05] Jonas Meyer: yes, we can surface kernel_id and execution_ms as attributes. those are helpful for correlating model slowdowns with specific kernels or compilation paths.
[00:04:15] Adeel Khan: on the networking side, for VPC or on-prem deployments how do you authenticate collectors?
[00:04:21] Samir Patel: we support a few modes: mTLS between collector and Redwood endpoint, short-lived signed tokens via KMS, or identity-based peering using cloud provider VPC peering plus private endpoints. we'll send a short runbook.
[00:04:34] Adeel Khan: and are traces stored encrypted at rest? any HSM integration?
[00:04:38] Samir Patel: yes encrypted at rest using KMS; for on-prem we can integrate with customer HSMs and key-wrap policies.
[00:04:46] Maya Chen: how does tracing affect cost? our ops team is worried that token-level metrics will blow up ingest costs.
[00:04:53] Elena Ortiz: cost is driven by cardinality and sampling rate. we suggest a multi-tier strategy: low-cardinality attributes always on, mid-cardinality via sampling, and payloads only for sampled traces. Redwood's Optimize module can recommend sampling thresholds based on cost/latency targets.
[00:05:10] Carlos Ruiz: OK practical — can you show an example dashboard we'd run post-collector?
[00:05:15] Elena Ortiz: Sure — panel 1: token cost by route (tokens generated * unit cost), panel 2: p50/p95/p99 latency with batch_size heatmap, panel 3: KV cache hit rate and miss latency, panel 4: quant_level vs eval_score scatter. i'll attach json panels.
[00:05:33] Maya Chen: Awesome. also we want an alert when kv_cache_miss_rate > 5% for 5m AND p99 latency increases 20% — possible?
[00:05:41] Jonas Meyer: yes, that's a composite alert. use metrics derived from traces and real-time logs. we recommend a rolling window and alert burn-in to avoid flapping.
[00:05:52] Carlos Ruiz: CRITICAL — testing plan: we'd like a 1-hour run that simulates 60K tokens/min with mixed prompt sizes. can Redwood run that in dedicated env so we can get clean numbers?
[00:06:02] Samir Patel: yes we can spin a dedicated bench. we'll need your prompt set and desired concurrency. we'll also mirror your Redis setup if you want realistic cache effects.
[00:06:14] Maya Chen: governance question: do we need to send raw tokens to Redwood for token-level analysis? we prefer aggregated metrics only.
[00:06:21] Elena Ortiz: you can run the collector on-prem and only export aggregated metrics — no raw tokens leave your VPC. or use hashed token buckets for frequency analysis. we'll document both flows.
[00:06:33] Adeel Khan: legal will want the list of exporters and retention policies.
[00:06:36] Samir Patel: we'll send the security pack with retention options and default 90-day retention and the ability to configure longer for enterprise.
[00:06:44] Carlos Ruiz: earlier you mentioned tail-sampling. how much memory does the collector need for tail-sampling window? we've had spikes.
[00:06:52] Jonas Meyer: it's proportional to the sampling window and throughput. for 60K tokens/min and 1.5K traces/min you might need a few GBs of RAM; we'll give a sizing table.
[00:07:03] Maya Chen: Anything else on quantization? we saw a small drop in token-level semantic accuracy when switching to 4-bit for certain prompts.
[00:07:11] Samir Patel: that's expected. best practice: run A/B with evaluation prompts instrumented as heldout traces. emit eval_score per rollout and have automatic rollback if quality drops beyond threshold.
[00:07:22] Priya Nair: can dashboards link back to raw trace snippets for investigation?
[00:07:26] Elena Ortiz: Yes, with sampling you can attach raw snippets for sampled traces. for PII, snippets are redacted by default.
[00:07:34] Carlos Ruiz: thanks. summary and next steps please.
[00:07:36] Samir Patel: recap — Redwood to share OTEL span schema, collector configs, dashboard examples, and security pack. Verdant to provide prompt set and SLO targets. We'll schedule the 1-hour dedicated benchmark, then follow-up to review.
[00:07:50] Maya Chen: perfect. thanks everyone.
[00:07:55] Elena Ortiz: i'll drop the panel jsons and a short how-to in the thread.
[00:07:59] Jonas Meyer: and I'll add kernel_id sampling notes to the schema doc.
[00:08:05] End of recording
notes: Spans: prefer enriched attributes over span-per-token to control volume
Use hybrid sampling (head + tail) to retain p99 outliers
KV cache events should include key_bucket and latency_ms
Quant_level should be a top-level attribute for rollout comparisons
Collector sizing depends on throughput; provide sizing table before benchmark
